app.title: ProteoClinView
app.summary: A person enters a protein sequence, either a demo protein or a pasted one, and picks which fragment ion series and charge states to predict. Then they bring in a spectrum: a synthetic demo, an example mzML file, or their own mzML upload, from which they pick one MS2 scan. They also set a mass tolerance in ppm. The interface computes the theoretical fragments and matches them to the measured peaks. It shows how many ions matched and how much of the sequence they cover, on a residue map linked to the annotated spectrum. A mirror plot sets measured against predicted peaks with the mass error of each peak, and the matched ions or the full fragment table can be downloaded as CSV.

task.text: Check how well a measured fragment spectrum supports a given protein sequence, by matching predicted fragment ions to observed peaks and showing which residues they cover.

data.text: A protein's amino acid sequence, the theoretical fragment ions computed from it, and a measured tandem mass spectrum given as peaks of m/z and intensity, from an mzML file or a pasted peak list.
data.item: a predicted fragment ion of the sequence, matched or not to a measured peak

stage.text: validating a protein identification against its fragment spectrum, after acquisition and search

mechanism.text: Settings in a sidebar (sequence, ion series, charges, spectrum source, tolerance) feed one computation that predicts fragments and matches them to peaks. A residue coverage map and the annotated spectrum are cross-linked, so clicking a residue highlights its peaks and clicking a peak highlights the residues it covers. A mirror plot with hover details and two tables report the matches, and both tables export as CSV.

field.text: fragment ion annotation of tandem mass spectra in top-down proteomics

workflow.name: match observed peaks to values predicted from a known template and report coverage

steps.here: Pick a demo protein or paste a single-letter sequence (unknown residues are rejected). Then choose a synthetic demo spectrum, the example mzML, an uploaded mzML or a pasted peak list, and pick one MS2 scan by scan id, RT, precursor and peak count.

steps.step: set what to predict and how strictly to match
steps.here: Checkboxes for c, z, b and y ion series, a slider for maximum charge, and a slider for mass tolerance in ppm.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Predicts monoisotopic fragment m/z for each series and charge, matches each one to the nearest peak within the tolerance, and reports matched ions and the fraction of residues covered.
A coverage map of the residues is cross-linked to the annotated spectrum: clicking a residue highlights its peaks, and clicking a peak shows its m/z, intensity and assigned ion.
A mirror plot puts the measured spectrum above the axis and the predicted ions below it, with matched ions solid and coloured by series, unmatched ones dotted, and the ppm error shown on hover.
Download the matched ions (theoretical and experimental m/z, Δppm, intensity, covered sequence) or the full fragment table as CSV.

distinctive: Predictions come from the sequence itself: cumulative residue masses give N-terminal and C-terminal fragment series at several charge states
Matching uses a relative mass tolerance in ppm, and every match reports its error in ppm
Coverage is counted per residue, so the result is how much of the template the matched pieces explain, not just how many peaks matched
A synthetic spectrum with dropped peaks, small m/z error and noise peaks lets the workflow run before any real data exists
The sequence, ion series and charges carry over from the coverage page to the mirror-plot page
